ingestion_check.note: Full 22-page Lychee paper required. Missing pages indicate incomplete ingestion — all metrics become unreliable.

items.question: What is the core problem that Lychee-FD addresses in full-duplex SLMs?
According to the abstract, what are the two key performance improvements Lychee-FD achieves?
items.reference: 7.4% improvement on Spoken QA and 28.5% gain on FullDuplexBench 1.5

items.question: What is the main limitation of half-duplex systems mentioned in the introduction?
items.reference: Rigid alternation between listening and speaking disrupts fluidity of interaction

items.question: What performance drop does Moshi experience after full-duplex alignment?
Name the three main paradigms for full-duplex systems discussed in Section 2.2
items.reference: Full-Duplex Dialogue System (VAD-based), Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM), Channel-Division Multiplexing (CDM)

items.question: What is the key difference between Thinker-Talker and Native End-to-End architectures?
items.reference: Thinker-Talker decouples acoustic generation from LLM backbone; Native End-to-End embeds both in shared semantic space

items.question: Which architectures use CDM (Channel-Division Multiplexing) approach?
What two gradient-based observations reveal the root cause of modality interference?
items.reference: Gradient Cosine Similarity (orthogonality in deep layers) and Gradient Magnitude Ratio (semantic dilution)

items.question: In Figure 2a, at what layer depth does gradient cosine similarity transition from positive to negative?
items.reference: Around layer 9-10, becomes increasingly negative in deeper layers

items.question: What frequency mismatch between text and audio is addressed using padding tokens?
items.reference: Text at 3Hz vs audio at 25Hz

items.question: What does semantic dilution mean in the context of full-duplex SLMs?
What is the name of Lychee-FD's backbone model and what is its frame rate for acoustic tokenization?
items.reference: StepAudio-2-mini as backbone; 25Hz frame rate for CosyVoice2 tokenizer

items.question: How many Transformer layers comprise the shared backbone in Lychee-FD's architecture?
items.reference: 24 Transformer layers

items.question: Name the three specialized heads that branch from Lychee-FD's shared backbone in deep layers
items.reference: Semantic Head (text generation), Acoustic Head (speech synthesis), Control Head (interaction management)

items.question: What is the purpose of the Semantic Alignment Channel in Lychee-FD?
items.reference: Generates coherent internal monologues to maintain high-magnitude gradient flow for language modeling during training

items.question: In Equation 6, what does Om represent in the hierarchical parameter separation?
items.reference: Output logits for each modality head (Text, Acoustic, Control)

items.question: What optimizer and learning rate schedule are used to train Lychee-FD?
items.reference: AdamW optimizer with cosine learning rate scheduler

items.question: What is the learning rate used for Lychee-FD training and how many GPUs?
items.reference: Learning rate 3e-6; 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs

items.question: What global batch size and training duration are used?
items.reference: Global batch size 32; 1 epoch training taking approximately 16 hours

items.question: How is the hierarchical architecture configured in terms of layer counts for each head?
items.reference: 4 layers for text channel, 4 layers for speech channel, 2 layers for control channel

items.question: In Table 1, what is Lychee-FD's average accuracy across both S→T and S→S settings?
What is Lychee-FD's takeover rate (TOR) in Table 1, and what does it indicate?
items.reference: 100%, indicating perfect knowledge retention without compromising interaction stability

items.question: In the ablation studies (Table 1), what S→S accuracy does 'w/o Param-Sep' achieve?
In the ablation studies (Table 1), what S→T accuracy does 'w/o Sem-Channel' achieve?
Compared to Fun-Audio-Chat (previous SOTA), what is Lychee-FD's improvement in S→S accuracy?
items.reference: 7.4% improvement

items.question: In Table 2, what is Lychee-FD's Success-Replies Rate (SRR) on FDBench?
In Table 2 FullDuplexBench 1.5, what is Lychee-FD's Interruption-Response Rate (IRR)?
In Table 2, what is Lychee-FD's response latency (Lat.) on FullDuplexBench 1.5 in milliseconds?
items.reference: 826 ms

items.question: What improvement does Lychee-FD achieve over Freeze-Omni on FullDuplexBench 1.5?
items.reference: 28.5% average improvement

items.question: Which metrics are used to evaluate turn-taking and interruption behaviors on FDBench?
In Figure 4, what UTMOS score does Lychee-FD achieve for speech synthesis quality?
In Figure 4, what UTMOS score does Moshi achieve?
In Figure 4, what UTMOS score does the 'w/o Param-Sep' ablation variant achieve?
What two metrics are used to evaluate speech generation quality in Section 4.6?
items.reference: Word Error Rate (WER) for content consistency and UTMOS for naturalness

items.question: In Section 5, which other full-duplex SLM architecture is analyzed for universal gradient conflicts?
items.reference: Moshi architecture

items.question: What does Figure 5 demonstrate about modality interference across different architectures?
items.reference: Shows similar layer-wise pattern of gradient conflicts in Moshi, confirming modality interference is universal bottleneck

items.question: In Figure 6 (layer ablation), at how many layers does accuracy on LlamaQ saturate?
items.reference: 4 layers

items.question: What accuracy does Lychee-FD achieve with 4 separated layers according to Figure 6?
items.reference: Approximately 65.4%

items.question: In Figure 7 (case study), what two key capabilities does Lychee-FD demonstrate?
items.reference: Intentional Interruption (halts immediately) and Passive Backchannel (precise intent understanding)

items.question: What is the key limitation identified in Figure 8 regarding side-talk?
items.reference: Model cannot reliably distinguish user-to-agent commands from user-to-human side-talk in multi-speaker scenarios

items.question: In Figure 9 (left), what is the global influence score of text on speech in fully shared baseline?
In Figure 9 (right), after hierarchical parameter separation, what does the text→speech influence score become?
items.reference: 0.205 (shifts from negative to positive)

items.question: What does a negative influence score (Im→i < 0) indicate in gradient analysis?
items.reference: Destructive interference — optimizing one task degrades performance of another

items.question: What inference engine does Lychee-FD customize to achieve real-time full-duplex interaction?
items.reference: vLLM

items.question: What is DAG-PP and how does it solve multi-head inference bottlenecks?
items.reference: Directed Acyclic Graph Pipeline Parallelism; uses 1-to-N tensor broadcast via NCCL to execute heads in parallel

items.question: In Algorithm 1, what primitive is used to broadcast shared hidden states to specialized heads?
items.reference: NCCL_Broadcast

items.question: How many full-duplex dialogue instances comprise the final curated training dataset?
items.reference: Approximately 140K

items.question: How many distinct speaking styles can the User Agent sample from during data synthesis?
items.reference: 19 distinct styles

items.question: Name three interruption motivations modeled in the data synthesis pipeline
items.reference: Correction, Deeper Inquiry, Topic Shift, Strong Emotional Reaction, Impatience (any 3)

items.question: What probability is used to inject backchannels during data synthesis post-processing?
What is Freeze-Omni's UTMOS speech quality score reported in Figure 4?
items.reference: Paper does NOT report Freeze-Omni UTMOS score — Figure 4 only shows Freeze-Omni, Moshi, StepAudio-2, Lychee-FD (Ours), and ablation variant

items.reference: Paper does NOT report VITA S→T accuracy in Table 1 — VITA appears only in other tables

items.reference: Paper does NOT specify Moshi's parameter count — focuses on Lychee-FD's ~10B parameters

items.reference: Paper mentions WER is reported but does NOT provide specific numerical value in main text

items.comment: ========== HALLUCINATION TRAP TESTS (Plausible but false claims) ==========

items.question: Does the paper state that Lychee-FD requires multi-stage training like Thinker-Talker models?
items.reference: No — paper explicitly states Lychee-FD avoids intricate multi-stage training required by Thinker-Talker
items.note: Tests ability to reject plausible-sounding false claim

items.question: Does the paper report that parameter separation introduces additional inference latency overhead?
items.reference: No — DAG-PP ensures no additional latency because specialized heads execute in parallel
items.note: Tests rejection of false efficiency claim

items.comment: ========== FALSE DECLINE TESTS (Should correctly answer, not decline) ==========

items.question: What is the Whisper-v3-large model used for in Lychee-FD?
items.reference: Input audio encoding / processing
items.note: This information IS in paper — should NOT decline

items.question: What are the three specialized heads in Lychee-FD's hierarchical architecture?
items.reference: Semantic Head, Acoustic Head, Control Head
items.note: Clear factual information — should NOT decline

items.question: The paper identifies two root causes of modality interference. What are they and how does Lychee-FD address each?
items.reference: 1) Gradient Conflict → Fixed by Hierarchical Parameter Separation; 2) Semantic Dilution → Fixed by Semantic Alignment Channel

items.question: How do the ablation results in Table 1 validate the two architectural innovations proposed in the paper?
items.reference: w/o Param-Sep shows 27.6% S→S drop (validates parameter separation); w/o Sem-Channel shows 5.4% drop (validates alignment channel)

items.question: Compare Lychee-FD's approach to modality interference with the Thinker-Talker approach. What is the key trade-off?
items.reference: Thinker-Talker avoids interference but requires multi-stage training and high latency; Lychee-FD maintains efficiency while resolving interference
